audit.why: Level 1 skill, Gangplank from level 2, even at 4-5 and 6 where Explosive Cask lands, Gangplank from first item on — that matches 53.53% and matches the prose, which already frames 4-5 as the flip and 6 as his displacement window.
audit.corrected: Chart left as-is; full and content layers agree row for row.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike and phase text named the abilities but attached no timings, so 'respect the displacement' had nothing behind it.
audit.why: Explosive Cask is 100/85/70 and Body Slam is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12 — a near-flat 13s. Those two numbers are the entire rhythm of the lane after level 6.
audit.corrected: Body Slam's flat cooldown and Explosive Cask's 100s written into mid; Drunken Rage's 5s written into early and wants.you[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[2] told you to all-in 'while his W damage reduction is on cooldown'. Drunken Rage is a 5-second cooldown — it is essentially never down, so that instruction describes a window that does not exist. Barrel Roll was also described as lobbing poke 'over the wall'; Riot's text is that he rolls the cask to a location, where it can be detonated early or explodes on its own after 4 seconds, growing in potency.
audit.why: Building a trade plan around waiting out a 5s cooldown loses the trade every time. The correct window is Body Slam's ~13s, and the correct answer to Drunken Rage is to trade through it with Grievous Wounds rather than to wait for it.
audit.corrected: wants.you[2] retargeted onto Body Slam's downtime and states the 5s; early describes the cask honestly, including that it hits harder the longer it brews.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's itemization already carries anti-heal, but the content layer never explained why, and Happy Hour was never named.
audit.why: Happy Hour heals Gragas periodically on skill use, so a poke-based win condition leaks value continuously without Grievous Wounds — this is the missing-interaction the brief flags as needs-antiheal.
audit.corrected: Happy Hour named in early and whys[5], with Grievous Wounds tied to it.

audit.why: All five packet suspectNames — 'His Explosive Cask', 'Powder Kegs', 'Lob Barrel Roll', 'Use Drunken Rage', 'His Barrel Roll' — are false positives. Every one is the correct Riot name with a leading word the matcher counted as edit distance.
audit.corrected: No name changes made on that basis.

edits.before: Stack your first item and use the keg-chain burst to win every all-in while his W damage reduction is on cooldown
edits.after: Stack your first item and use keg-chain burst on his Body Slam downtime — 13s — since Drunken Rage (W) is back every 5s

edits.before: Sheen/Essence Reaver empowers Parrrley and your keg chain bursts him through W damage reduction — force every all-in.
edits.after: Sheen/Essence Reaver empowers Parrrley and your keg chain bursts through Drunken Rage — bring Grievous Wounds for Happy Hour.

edits.before: Gragas owns these levels and you know it. His Barrel Roll (Q) lobs free poke and a slow over the wall while you can only last-hit, and he can walk up to auto your single low-HP Powder Keg off the map, denying the barrel you need to scale. Do not place a keg where he can casually pop it; hold E for waveclear or to threaten his all-in. Last-hit with the tip of Parrrley, eat the Q chip, and refuse to trade autos into his W (Drunken Rage) damage-reduction-and-sustain window — that drink heals him through anything short. Your job here is just to not die and not get barrels denied.
edits.after: Gragas owns these levels and you know it. Barrel Roll (Q) rolls a cask at 850 to your 625 and he can detonate it early or let it sit — it hits harder the longer it brews — and he can walk up to auto your single low-HP Powder Keg off the map, denying the barrel you need to scale. Don't place a keg where he can casually pop it. Last-hit at the tip of Parrrley, eat the Q chip, and refuse auto trades into Drunken Rage (W): that drink is a 5s cooldown, cuts the damage you deal and, with Happy Hour, heals him through anything short. Just don't die and don't get barrels denied.

edits.before: This is where the lane flips. At 4-5 your second Q and E points let you land Parrrley-into-keg poke from outside his Body Slam (E) range, so he takes chip every time he walks up to farm while you stay safe behind the barrel slow. The danger is his level-6 Explosive Cask: if he hits 6 first he can Body Slam in and R-knock you into his tower or punt you off your own keg cluster, so respect the displacement and don't over-extend on a chain. Bait his E engage, sidestep the cask, then detonate your keg chain on top of him as he commits and burns W.
edits.after: This is where the lane flips. At 4-5 your second Q and E points let you poke Parrrley-into-keg from outside Body Slam's 600 range, so he takes chip every walk-up while you sit behind the barrel slow. Body Slam barely scales — 14s at rank 1, 12s at rank 5 — so its downtime is your whole trading window. The danger is level 6: Explosive Cask on 100s can knock you into his tower or punt you off your own keg cluster. Bait the E engage, sidestep the cask, then detonate the chain on top of him as he commits and burns his drink.

notes: The worst error here was advice, not naming: wants.you[2] told the player to all-in when Gragas's damage reduction was on cooldown, but Drunken Rage is 5s and is effectively always available. Retargeted onto Body Slam's ~13s. All five flagged suspect names were false positives. The full layer's dosFull[0] still says 'Q-cleanse the slow' about Body Slam — Body Slam stuns, it does not slow; Barrel Roll is the slow. I left it because Remove Scurvy is W, not Q, so that line has a second error in it and the whole entry needs rewriting rather than patching; flagging instead.
